svg.title: How an AI agent works
svg.desc: The context window of an AI agent: what is always loaded, what loads on demand through tool calls, and what runs in a separate window, with zoomed panels on token-by-token writing, tool calls, MCP, subagents, recall and what carries over between sessions.
svg.text: The model reads text and images and writes text. The harness, the program around the model, decides what the model reads, and acts on what the model writes.
What the model reads during one task
Start here. Panels A to E show parts of it in more detail.
what the model reads for every reply
AGENTS.md: your project's rules, full text
Memory index: one line per saved note
Skill list: a name and a description per skill
Tool list: Read, Edit, Bash, Agent, MCP tools

how much the model thinks and
Reads all the text in the
Model or harness? Claude Opus is a
model and Claude Code is a harness.
Pi and OpenCode are harnesses that
can run Claude, GPT, Gemini or
read in full for every token*
Always: sent with every request, from the first one.
On demand: added when the model calls a tool, and kept until compaction.
Isolated: done in another window. Only a summary comes back.
* The model uses every earlier token for each new one, but it does not process them again. During the reply it keeps that work, and between requests the provider's
cache keeps it while the start of the window stays the same (see part 2). [7]
Model: the neural network that reads text and images and writes
text, for example Claude Opus, GPT or Gemini. Open-weight
models such as Qwen or DeepSeek can also run on your own
Harness: the program around the model. It builds the context
window, sends it to the model, runs the tools and asks for your
permission. For example Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI,
Agent: a model and a harness in a loop: the model writes tool
calls, and the harness runs them and adds the results, until the
Provider: the company that runs the model on its servers, for
example Anthropic, OpenAI or Google. It bills per token, or per
month with limits counted in tokens.
Token: a word or a piece of a word. 1,000 tokens are roughly 550
to 750 English words, depending on the model. [1, 2]
Context window: all the text the model reads to write its next
reply. Its size has a limit, for example 1,000,000 tokens.
Session: one conversation with its own context window. A new
session starts with an empty conversation.
Skill: a folder with instructions in a SKILL.md file. The model reads
the file with a tool call when a task needs it.
MCP: a standard way for a harness to use tools from other
Training: how a model is built, from text collected up to a cutoff
date. The model does not change while you use it.
At the start, the harness asks each MCP server for its list of
It adds each tool to the tool list in the window, with its
description. Claude Code adds only the names, and adds a
description when the model searches for that tool. [12]
When the model calls one, the harness passes the call to that
server and adds the answer to the window. [11]
MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard plug, so any harness
can use any MCP server. To the model, an MCP tool is one more
A subagent is a second conversation that the harness runs, with
its own window and the same model or another one. A standard
subagent gets only the task text, so the task must contain all the
details. A fork gets a copy of your conversation. [13]
The file reads stay in the subagent's window, and only its
Why use one? A big search can fill a window with file text. In
a subagent, that text stays out of your window, so yours
stays short. The reads still cost tokens. [13]
Agents in a team exchange messages the same way: the harness
adds each message as new text to the other agent's window.
Agents can also share a task list in a file on disk. In Claude Code,
agent teams are experimental and off by default. [14]
and so on, one step per token, until the reply or a tool call is done.
To pick each next token, the model uses all the tokens before it:
the set-up text, the conversation, the tool output and its own
new words. It keeps its work on earlier tokens, so it does not
process them again during the reply.
The model keeps no state between requests: for every reply it
reads the whole window again. Most harnesses send the whole
window each time, and some providers can keep it on their
Part 2 shows thinking, effort, caching and price in detail.
A tool call is just text
The model cannot run anything itself. It writes a tool call, in the
format that the tool list describes:
I will follow the debug skill first.
Find: the provider's software finds the call in the output,
much like grep, ends the reply there and sends the call to
Run: the harness runs the matching program, here a file
read. It can ask you for permission first.
Add: the harness adds the program's output to the window
Repeat: the harness sends the longer window, and the
Some tools, such as web search, run at the provider instead, and
the provider adds their results to the window. [10]
A skill loads the same way: the model reads its SKILL.md file
Details used correctly, by amount of text
The curve is illustrative, not measured data.
All tokens share the model's attention. The fuller the window, the
more often a detail is missed or mixed up. [15, 16] Models from
2023 also missed more in the middle of a long window than at
So agents load text only when needed and give big searches to
subagents. A new task is better done in a new session.
Compaction. When the window is almost full, the harness
replaces the old conversation with a short summary. Details
that are not in the summary are lost. [3]
What carries over to the next session
Only files carry over, so to keep a lesson for later sessions, write
it in a file that the harness loads. [4]

project" (code.claude.com/docs/en/memory); [5] Anthropic, "Agent Skills" (platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview); [6] Anthropic, "Effort" (platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort); [7] Anthropic, "Prompt caching" (platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching); [8] OpenAI, "Reasoning models"

(developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning); [9] Google, "Gemini thinking" (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thinking); [10] Anthropic, "Tool use" (platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview); [11] Model Context Protocol specification, "Tools" (modelcontextprotocol.io/specification); [12] Claude Code docs, "Connect Claude Code to

tools via MCP" (code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp); [13] Claude Code docs, "Create custom subagents" (code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents); [14] Claude Code docs, "Orchestrate teams of Claude Code sessions" (code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams); [15] Anthropic, "Effective context engineering for AI agents" (2025, anthropic.com/engineering); [16] Chroma,
"Context Rot" (2025, research.trychroma.com/context-rot); [17] Liu et al., "Lost in the Middle" (TACL 2024, arxiv.org/abs/2307.03172). Chart shapes are illustrative.
